events.name: The Lights Went Out
events.intro: Dusk comes down, and the next town on your map does not answer it. No street lamps. No kitchen windows. You walk in past dark shopfronts and hear only your own steps. At the edge of the square a man in a hi-vis vest is bent over a dead generator, a torch clamped in his teeth, both hands deep in the wiring. Teague, around the torch: "Don't touch that, it bites." He spits the torch into his palm. "Whole grid's down. Third night. Something's draining it faster than I can fix it." He looks toward the one building on the hill that still has a dim glow in it. "Whatever it is, it's getting worse. Hospital's on backup. Backup lasts two more days."

success.text: Teague points his torch along a fat black cable that runs out of the square and into the trees. "Follow that. Whatever's drinking the grid is at the other end of it." For the first time in three nights he sounds like a man who might sleep.

Your Electric-type looks up at the hill, then at you, and goes without being asked twice. Nurses wheel a cable out to meet it. One ward at a time, the windows come back, and somebody inside starts to cry with relief. It will be tired for a while. Nobody on that hill will forget who it was.

effects.label: Lent to the hospital: your Electric-types fight at half strength

success.text: Teague nods as if he expected it, and puts the torch back between his teeth. You are three streets away when the glow on the hill flickers once, and steadies, and you find that you are counting the seconds until it does. The dark town stays on your map behind you.

events.name: The Tap
events.intro: The cable runs a mile through wet bracken to a fenced substation, humming where it should be silent. Someone has cut the padlock. Behind the transformers a pump the size of a wardrobe is bolted straight onto the main line, and its dials are all pinned to the right. Two Grunts sit on upturned crates beside it, sharing a flask, watching a town's worth of light pour into a row of unmarked batteries.

success.text: One of them sees you and drops the flask. "Kid. Walk away. This is above you." Neither of them walks away either.

win.text: You pulled the tap off the grid. For one hour, the dark town had its lights back

choices.label: Mark the place for Teague and go.

success.text: You scratch the turning onto your map and carry it back. Teague stares at it for a long time. "A tap. Right on the main. I'd never have looked there." The pump keeps running tonight, but now somebody knows where it is.

events.name: Hospital or Dam
events.intro: Your radio spits static, then a voice you know. Teague, on the radio: "Hospital's out. And the dam's floodgates are electric. They're stuck shut and the river's rising." Behind his voice you can hear people shouting, and under them, water. Teague: "You can get to one of them before it's bad. Not both."

success.text: You run for the hill. Your team lights the wards by hand, by spark, by anything, and every patient comes through the night. The dam is cranked open late, by farmers with a tractor chain. The valley holds, but one farm on the low bank goes under. You will see that family at the next Pokémon Center, sitting very straight on a bench with one bag between the four of them, and the mother will thank you for the hospital and mean it.

You run for the river. The gates grind open a hand's width at a time, and the valley below never knows how close it came. On the hill, the hospital goes dark for one hour. Nurse Joy finds you herself the next morning. She is not angry. "Everyone came through but one. An old Chansey of ours. She had worked here longer than I have." She presses your hand. "You saved a valley. I wanted you to hear it from me, and not from somebody who would make it sound like blame."

You split your team down the middle and send half of your heart up the hill. Three for the wards. Three for the gates. Nobody rests, and nobody is coming to relieve them. If both halves hold, both places are saved.

win.text: You split your team between the hospital and the dam, and both held. Nobody was lost that night

lose.text: You split your team between the hospital and the dam, and one half could not hold. The town carries what that cost

remembers.intro: Your radio spits static, then a voice you know. Teague, on the radio: "Hospital's holding. Your Electric-type did that, three nights ago. They've still got a charge in the wards." Then, faster: "But the dam's floodgates are electric. They're stuck shut and the river's rising." Under his voice you can hear the water. For once, there is only one place you have to be.

success.text: You run for the river with nothing behind you to fear for. The gates grind open a hand's width at a time. Down the valley, lamps you lit days ago are still burning on the hill, and by morning the river is back between its banks. Teague finds you at the gate wheel and just grips your shoulder. Nobody was lost. Not one.

remembers.notice: Your ally has the radio pressed to one ear. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: You take your place, and across the valley someone else takes theirs. Wards light. Gates turn. When the sun comes up there is a hospital full of people arguing about breakfast and a river running exactly where a river should. Teague sits down on his dead generator and laughs until he has to take his glasses off.

You take your place, and across the valley someone else takes theirs. Wards light. Gates turn. When the sun comes up there is a hospital full of people arguing about breakfast and a river running exactly where a river should. Teague sits down on his dead generator and laughs until he has to take his glasses off.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: The two of you take the hill at a run. Something in the dark ward corridors has been driven wild by the surges, and it is between you and the generator room.
The two of you take the river road at a run. The surges have maddened everything that nests in the dam's wiring, and it is all between you and the gate wheel.

events.name: The Dark Town
events.intro: The glow on the hill is gone. You notice it the way you notice a clock that has stopped: late, and all at once. Word comes down the road with a pedlar. The backup ran dry. The grid never came back. They moved the patients out by cart, by torchlight, three towns over.

success.text: The town will be dark for as long as you are in this region. Shutters stay down on the shops, and the places where a traveller could rest have less to give than they did. Teague is still out there with his torch. He does not blame you. That is the part that stays with you.

effects.label: The dark town: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The blackout was never mended. A whole town went dark for the region

events.name: The River Is Rising
events.intro: Brown water lies across the road where the road used to be. Families wade uphill with chairs over their heads and children on their hips. A soaked Psyduck sits on a floating door, turning in a slow circle, holding its head. A woman pushes a pram past you, and the pram is full of photographs. Ada: "It's never come this high. Not in my lifetime." She does not stop walking. "The weir upstream's blocked. Something's dammed it. The water can't get out."

success.text: Ada looks at you properly for the first time. "Upstream. Past the old logging track. If you can open it, all of this drains by morning." She says it the way people say things they have stopped letting themselves hope for.

You spend the day as a pair of arms. A cot. A grandfather. A crate of hens. Ada's pram, the last and heaviest, lifted over the wall with every photograph dry. By dusk her whole family is counted twice on the hilltop, and the water has not gained an inch on anyone you carried.

It lets you lift it off the door without a sound and clamps both arms around your neck. "That's my grandson's," Ada calls back. "He's on the hill. Keep hold of it till this is done, would you?" The Psyduck looks up at the grey sky, visibly thinking about rain, at the worst possible moment. You can tell this will not be the last time.

remembers.notice: You already know what is up there. Faulk, the banker you pulled off his door of a raft, saw it from the bridge before the bridge went: a logging crew's debris, jammed across the weir like a cork.

success.text: You do not need to search for it. You take the logging track straight to the jam Faulk described, and your team has the first trunks loose before the light goes. The water behind it drops a hand. It is a start, and it is a day sooner than anyone could have asked for.

events.name: The Weir
events.intro: Upstream the river is a brown lake, and the weir is the wall holding it there. It is not stone that blocks the sluice. It is timber: fresh-cut trunks with a logging crew's paint on the ends, washed down from an Evil Team clearing and wedged in a mass no wider than a barn door. Beyond it you can see the roofs of the upstream village, half of each one, and people on them.

success.text: The trunks are slick and the current wants your legs. Things that lived in that clearing came down with the wood, frightened and furious, and they are not ready to be moved either.

win.text: You broke the timber jam at the weir, and the flood began to drain

success.text: The jam can wait an hour. The people on the roofs cannot. Your team ferries them across to the high bank one and two at a time: a baker with her cat in a flour sack, a boy who will not let go of a school atlas. The water is still rising when you finish. Nobody on those roofs is in it.

events.name: School or Shelter
events.intro: It starts as a sound like a long freight train. Then the weir breaks. Water comes down the valley in a wall, carrying fence posts and a whole henhouse on its shoulder. Ada, shouting from the hill with both hands round her mouth: "The school's on the low road! And the Pokémon shelter!" Two roofs. Two directions. The wall of water does not care which you pick.

success.text: You reach the school with the water at your knees and leave with it at your chest, and every child is on the hill by nightfall, every one, counted by a teacher who cannot stop counting. The shelter's Pokémon had nobody. They swam for it. Most made the bank. Three were taken by the river, and nobody knows where it put them down. Far downstream, frightened things that used to have names will be learning to be wild.

You reach the shelter as the pens start to float. Your team opens every latch, and every Pokémon in that building rides out on somebody's back, down to an old Meowth with three legs. The school's roof holds. The children wait on it until a boat can come, hours late, cold and silent and frightened, and every single one of them alive. A girl wrapped in a blanket asks you if the Pokémon are all right. You get to tell her yes.

Three to the school. Three to the shelter. You stand on the bank between them where you can see both roofs and help neither, and you call your orders across the water. If both halves hold against the river, both roofs empty in time.

win.text: You split your team between the school and the shelter, and the river took nobody

lose.text: You split your team between the school and the shelter, and the river was too strong for one half

remembers.notice: The Psyduck on your shoulder has stopped holding its head. It is staring at the wall of water with wide, calm eyes, and where it stares, the wave bends. It is using Confusion on the river itself.

success.text: Three to the school. Three to the shelter. The Psyduck stands on your head and pushes at the water with everything in its aching skull, and the wave that should have hit the shelter breaks around it instead. There is only one surge left to hold.

win.text: A borrowed Psyduck turned a flood aside, and the river took nobody

remembers.notice: Your ally is already knee-deep. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: You take one roof. Someone you trust takes the other. From the hill Ada watches two lines of small shapes climbing out of the water at once, children on one side and Pokémon on the other, and when the last of both is up she sits down in the mud beside her pram and opens it, and starts showing the photographs to anyone who will look.

You take one roof. Someone you trust takes the other. From the hill Ada watches two lines of small shapes climbing out of the water at once, children on one side and Pokémon on the other, and when the last of both is up she sits down in the mud beside her pram and opens it, and starts showing the photographs to anyone who will look.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: The two of you wade for the school together. The flood has thrown every panicked thing in the river against its doors.
The two of you wade for the shelter together. The flood has thrown every panicked thing in the river against its doors.

events.name: The Drowned Valley
events.intro: The weir went in the night, with nobody there. You hear it from a ferryman poling across what used to be a street. The school is a roof. The shelter is a roof. Everyone got out, he thinks. Almost everyone. He does not finish the thought.

success.text: The valley will be under water for as long as you are in this region. People got out with what they could carry, and they are sleeping in barns on the hills. Ada waves to you from one. She is holding the pram handle with both hands. You wave back, and keep walking, and it is the hardest road you have walked.

effects.label: The drowned valley: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The flood was never stopped. A valley went under

events.name: Downstream
events.intro: A new region, a new riverbank, and something watching you from the reeds. It is thin, and it flinches at the sound of the water. Around its neck is a strip of blue cloth, the kind a shelter ties on so it can tell its animals apart. It came a long way on a flood you remember. It has not let anyone near it since.

success.text: You sit on the bank with your back to it and do nothing at all. An hour. Two. Something cold touches your elbow. When you look down it is pressed against your side, shaking, with its eyes shut tight. You untie the wet cloth and put it in your pocket. It has a name on it. You will use it.

You set down what you can spare on a flat stone and walk on without looking back, so that it will dare to come out. At the bend in the path you look back anyway. It is eating. It is still alone. But tonight it is not hungry, and that is one thing set right.

events.name: Smoke on the Horizon
events.intro: Black smoke stands over the fields like a second, wrong sky. At the factory gate, workers in overalls are waving at the road with both arms, at anyone, at you. Their foreman meets you at a run. Rosa: "A vat's cracked. It's leaking into the canal and the vents are jammed." She drags a sleeve across her eyes and leaves a clean stripe. "Three of mine are still inside. The owner says wait for the fire crew. The fire crew's two hours away."

success.text: Rosa shoves a wet rag into your hand. "Tie that on. Stay low. Left at the boilers." She grips your arm hard, once. "Their names are Bex, Olu and Gant. Shout them. They'll answer if they can."

The vent wheels are rusted solid, and they were never meant to be turned by anything smaller than a crane. Your Pokémon sets its shoulders against the first one. Metal screams. Then every louvre on the roof slams open together, and the smoke goes straight up in a column instead of out across the town. Rosa watches it rise. "That buys them air," she says. "That buys them an hour."

The vent wheels are rusted solid. Your Steel-type does not turn them. It simply walks into the first one, and keeps walking. Every louvre on the roof slams open together, and the smoke goes straight up in a column instead of out across the town. Rosa watches it rise. "That buys them air," she says. "That buys them an hour."

He is not hard to find. He is in the back of a long car at the side gate with the engine running, a briefcase on his knees, telling his driver to go. When you stand in front of the bonnet he sighs like a man delayed by weather, and sends his bodyguard's Pokémon out to move you.

win.text: The factory owner gave up the name of the chemical in the cracked vat

events.name: Inside the Factory
events.intro: Inside, the smoke is a ceiling at head height and dropping. Pipes tick and groan with heat. You shout the names. "Bex! Olu! Gant!" Somewhere past the boilers, someone bangs a wrench on a rail: three knocks, a gap, three knocks. Between you and the sound is a corridor you cannot see across and a run of pipework glowing a dull, dangerous red.

success.text: Your Flying-type beats its wings in the doorway until the smoke peels back down the corridor like a curtain. There they are, on the floor under the rail, rags over their faces. Gant cannot walk. Bex and Olu have not left him. You carry them out into a yard full of people who make a sound you will remember for the rest of your life.

Your Water-type plays a steady jet along the red pipework, and the red goes to grey, and the groaning stops. With the heat off, you can crawl the corridor on your elbows. There they are, under the rail, rags over their faces. Gant cannot walk. Bex and Olu have not left him. You bring out all three, and the yard makes a sound you will remember for the rest of your life.

No wings to clear it, no water to cool it. You go in with the rag over your mouth and your team pressed close, toward the knocking. It costs all of you. But you find the rail, and three people under it, and you do not come out until every one of them comes with you.

events.name: Canal or Well
events.intro: Rosa finds you with a map flapping in her fist. Her three are out. She has not stopped moving. Rosa: "We've got the three. But the canal goes to the marsh, and the town well's on the same line." She stabs two places on the map, a thumb apart and a mile from each other. There are enough sandbags, and enough of you, for one seal before the spill arrives.

success.text: You wall the canal off with sandbags and bodies and every Pokémon you have, and the black water stops a stone's throw short of the marsh. The reeds stay green. The things that live in them never know. In town, the well is capped with a painted warning, and for the rest of this region people queue for bottled water at a cart. It costs them. It will cost you too, a little, at every counter here.

effects.label: Bottled water: prices are up by a tenth

success.text: You cap the well-line with the spill a street away, and the town drinks clean tonight without ever knowing how near it was. The canal runs black all the way to the marsh. By the week's end the marsh Pokémon are sick: slow, dull-eyed, off their food. A ranger nails up a notice asking for anyone who can help. You read it twice.

Half your team to the canal bank, half to the well-line, and you running the mile between them with the map in your teeth. Poisoned things are coming up out of the water at both ends. If both halves hold, both seals close.

win.text: You sealed the canal and the well at once. The marsh and the town both drank clean

lose.text: You tried to seal the canal and the well at once, and one seal did not hold

remembers.notice: You have the chemical's name, the one the owner gave up beside his car. The clinic already has the right treatment on the boil. Whatever you cannot reach in time tonight can be put right within days, not seasons.

success.text: You wall off the canal, and the marsh stays green. The well is fouled, but the clinic knows exactly what fouled it. They dose the line by lamplight, and by the next stage of your road the town is drinking from it again. Rosa keeps the scrap of paper with the chemical's name on it folded in her breast pocket, like a thing that might be needed twice.

You cap the well-line, and the town drinks clean. The marsh takes the spill, but the clinic knows exactly what it is. Rangers wade out with the right medicine in backpacks, and by the next stage of your road the marsh Pokémon are eating again. Rosa keeps the scrap of paper with the chemical's name on it folded in her breast pocket, like a thing that might be needed twice.

remembers.notice: Your ally has already lifted the first sandbag. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: Two seals, a mile apart, closed in the same minute. The marsh stays green. The well stays sweet. Rosa walks the whole length of the canal that evening with her hands in her pockets, looking for a leak, and does not find one, and at the end of it she sits on the lock gate and lets her three sit with her.

Two seals, a mile apart, closed in the same minute. The marsh stays green. The well stays sweet. Rosa walks the whole length of the canal that evening with her hands in her pockets, looking for a leak, and does not find one, and at the end of it she sits on the lock gate and lets her three sit with her.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: You and your ally hit the canal bank together. Everything the spill has driven out of the water is coming up it toward you.
You and your ally reach the well-line together. Everything the spill has driven up out of the drains is between you and the valve.

events.name: Black Water
events.intro: The smoke is still standing over the fields when you next look back, days later. Nobody sealed anything. A carter tells you the canal ran black to the marsh and the well went the same week. He is hauling barrels of clean water in from two towns away, and charging for it, and not enjoying that.

success.text: For as long as you are in this region, the water here is not safe, and everything costs more because of it. Rosa got her three out. She says that to herself a lot, you are told. It is true. It was not enough, and she knows it, and so do you.

effects.label: Black water: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The factory spill was never sealed. The marsh and the town well were both lost

events.name: Something Is Making Pokémon Sick
events.intro: A ranger station with its door propped open. Inside, a ranger is asleep face-down on her desk with a pen still in her hand. On blankets along the wall lie three sick Pokémon, breathing fast and shallow. One of them, a Skitty, lifts its head when you come in and cannot hold it up. The ranger jerks awake. Ines: "Sorry. Sorry. Haven't slept." She rubs her face with both hands. "Same fever everywhere. Wild and owned. Starts as a cough. Then they won't eat." She looks at the blankets. "I think it's in the water. Or a Pokémon carrying it. I can't tell which and I can't test both."

success.text: Ines hands you three stoppered jars and a map with three streams circled. You fill one at each: the spring, the ford, the pond where everything drinks. Back at the station she holds each to the lamp and adds her drops, and waits, and all three stay clear. "Clean." She breathes out. "It isn't the water. That's half the question gone."

You follow the cough. A sick Rattata here, a wheezing Pidgey a mile on, each a little fresher than the last, a trail of small miseries pointing north. It ends at a stand of bare trees white with Swablu, a whole migrating flock, hundreds, and every one of them coughing like a tiny door creaking. They carried it in on the wind. They did not know. They look as sorry as anything you have ever seen.

You take the night shift so that Ines can sleep in a real bed. Cool cloths. Water from a spoon. The Skitty will not drink for her, but it drinks for you, a drop at a time, with one paw resting on your wrist as if to keep you there. By morning its breathing has slowed. It watches you pack with enormous eyes. It will know you again, anywhere.

remembers.intro: Ines has the jars lined up clear on one side of her desk and your map of the flock on the other. She is wide awake now. Ines: "Not the water. The Swablu. You've given me the whole answer." She is already pulling down books. "With both I can make the medicine properly. Give me until the roost is found again."

success.text: She does not look up when you go. On the blankets, the Skitty watches you all the way to the door.

remembers.intro: The station again. Three clear jars stand on the desk. Ines: "It isn't the water. So it's being carried. If someone could find what's carrying it..." She looks at the three on the blankets, and does not finish.

The station again. Ines has your sketch of the Swablu roost pinned over her desk. Ines: "A whole flock. Poor things." She frowns. "But if it's in the streams as well, curing the birds won't end it. I'd want the water ruled out."

events.name: The Cough
events.intro: One of your own team stops on the road and makes a small, dry, creaking sound. Then again. It looks up at you, embarrassed, as if it has done something wrong. It has not. It has only been walking beside you through a sick country.

success.text: You wrap it in your own jacket and slow your pace to match its pace. Ines told you the fever is never the end of anyone, only a long, tired week. It leans on your leg when you stop. It is slower. It is not leaving your side.

effects.label: The cough: your Pokémon are a little slower

events.name: Roost or Kennels
events.intro: Ines meets you on the station step with a single wooden case held against her chest like a child. Inside, in straw, are a dozen small brown bottles. Ines: "We've got enough medicine for one place. The flock's roost, or the town kennels." She has clearly been asking herself the same question all night, and is ashamed of how glad she is to hand it to someone else.

success.text: You carry the case to the bare trees and dose the Swablu one by one, hundreds of small beaks, until the bottles are empty and the creaking in the branches has gone quiet. The fever ends where it began. In town, the kennel Pokémon get better the slow way, on rest and broth, over weeks. Two of their owners find you in the street. One shouts. One just asks why the birds came first, and waits for an answer, holding a lead with nobody on the end of it.

You carry the case into town, and by evening every pet in the kennels has had its dose and is asleep with a full belly for the first time in days. A small boy sits with his Lillipup's head in his lap and will not be moved. Out at the bare trees, the flock lifts on the next north wind, still coughing. It will come down again a region further on. You will be there to hear it.

Ines counts the bottles into two rows with her lips moving. Half doses. Half for the birds, half for the pets. Getting it into a frightened flock and a frightened kennel on the same day takes every member of your team, and the sick do not always know that you are helping.

win.text: You split the medicine between the roost and the kennels. Both mended, slowly

win.label: The cough: your Pokémon are a little slower

lose.text: You split the medicine between the roost and the kennels, and could not get it all where it was needed

success.text: Ines counts the bottles into two rows, half doses, not enough. Then your Pokémon lifts its head and rings. The sound goes through the station like clean water. On the blankets, three sick heads come up at once. "Do that at the roost," Ines whispers. "Do that at the kennels." A half dose and a Heal Bell, it turns out, is a whole cure. Nobody pays anything for it at all.

remembers.intro: Ines meets you on the station step with two wooden cases, one under each arm, grinning like someone who has not grinned in a month. Ines: "You ruled out the water and you found the flock. I knew exactly what I was making. So I made it twice." There is nothing to choose. There is only the carrying.

success.text: The roost in the morning: hundreds of small beaks, and then quiet in the branches. The kennels by evening: a boy asleep on the floor with his Lillipup asleep on top of him. Two empty cases. Ines writes the recipe out three times and posts it to three other stations before she lets herself sit down.

remembers.notice: Your ally has taken the second strap of the case without being asked. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: Two cases go out of the station door that morning in two directions. By nightfall the branches at the roost are quiet, and the kennels are full of sleeping animals, and Ines is asleep on her desk again with the pen in her hand. This time nobody wakes her.

Two cases go out of the station door that morning in two directions. By nightfall the branches at the roost are quiet, and the kennels are full of sleeping animals, and Ines is asleep on her desk again with the pen in her hand. This time nobody wakes her.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: You carry the case to the roost with your ally beside you.
You carry the case to the kennels with your ally beside you.

events.name: The Long Fever
events.intro: Another station, another ranger, the same cough behind the door. The fever outran everyone. This one tells you Ines is still working, three valleys back, on a medicine for a sickness that has already moved on.

success.text: For as long as you are in this region, something will always be coughing: in a hedge, in a kennel, at your own heel. It is never the end of anyone. It is only a whole country that is tired, and takes longer to mend than it should have.

effects.label: The cough: your Pokémon are a little slower
The long fever: healing items restore a quarter less

effects.text: The fever was never stopped. It ran through the whole region

events.name: The Flock Comes Down
events.intro: A new region. A fence along the road with a line of small white shapes on the top rail, and before you are close enough to count them you hear it: a tiny, creaking, apologetic cough, a hundred times over. The Swablu know you. They shuffle along the rail to make room, as if you had come to sit with them.

success.text: The ranger here has never heard of Ines or her medicine. You draw the roost, and the bottles, and write down the station's name, and she pins it over her desk with a face that says she understands exactly what is about to begin. It begins a little sooner here because of a choice you made. It will end sooner too, because you said so.

events.name: Pyromaniac Sweep
events.intro: A field is burning in a line too straight to be an accident. At the far end of it a figure with a torch looks back at the flames, laughs, and runs into the smoke. A farmer stumbles out of the stubble beating at his sleeve. Farmer: "That's the third one! He's lighting them on purpose!" He turns his wet face into the wind and goes still. "The wind's turning toward the orchard village."

success.text: You go into the smoke after the laugh. He is waiting on the far side with the torch still lit and a uniform under his coat, delighted to have an audience.

win.text: You caught the man lighting the fields. He was following orders, and he said whose

success.text: Your team lays water down the burning line again, and again, and a third time, steam rolling over all of you, until the last of it hisses out a stride from the farmer's barn. This field, at least, will be ploughed in spring. He cannot speak. He just holds his hat against his chest.

You outrun the wind by minutes. Bells. Doors. Carts filled with grandmothers and ladders and caged birds. When the smoke reaches the first orchard wall, there is nobody left behind it to breathe it. Whatever the fire takes from this village now, it will not be a person.
You go into the smoke after the laugh. He is waiting on the far side with the torch still lit and a uniform under his coat, delighted to have an audience.

events.name: Village or Station
events.intro: Two columns of smoke now, one on each side of the valley. Under the left one is the orchard village, its trees going up like matches in a row. Under the right is the Ranger station, and the long shed behind it where they keep every hurt and orphaned animal for miles. A ranger on the road grabs your arm. "There's one pump cart. One. Where do we take it?"

success.text: The pump cart goes left. You save the houses, the well, and half the orchard, and old people stand in the lane touching their own front doors. The Ranger station burns to its stone footings. The rangers got the shed open in time and drove everything out ahead of the flames. The animals lived. They are scattered over three hills now, hurt and frightened, and it will take a season to find them all.

The pump cart goes right. You hold the fire at the station fence, and behind it the long shed stays standing with every hurt creature safe inside. The orchard village burns. Its people are alive, on the road, with what they could carry. An old man looks back at the glow and says his grandfather planted those trees, and then says nothing else for a very long time.

You send three to the orchard wall and three to the station fence, with buckets where there is no pump. The fire has driven every wild thing in the valley mad with fear, and they are between your team and the flames. If both halves hold, both fires stop.

win.text: You fought two fires at once, and both the village and the station were standing at dawn

lose.text: You fought two fires at once, and one of them won

remembers.notice: The village is already empty. You saw to that, the day you outran the wind. Whatever burns there tonight is timber and fruit, and not one person.
Your ally is tying a wet cloth over their face. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: One of you at the orchard wall, one at the station fence, and the pump cart running between on a road cleared by rangers. At dawn both columns of smoke have thinned to nothing. The village still has its trees. The shed still has its animals. The farmer whose field started all this walks the lane handing out apples, because he has to give somebody something.

One of you at the orchard wall, one at the station fence, and the pump cart running between on a road cleared by rangers. At dawn both columns of smoke have thinned to nothing. The village still has its trees. The shed still has its animals. The farmer whose field started all this walks the lane handing out apples, because he has to give somebody something.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: You and your ally run the pump cart toward the village. Everything the fire has driven out of the orchard is stampeding down the lane.
You and your ally run the pump cart toward the station. Everything the fire has driven out of the woods is stampeding through the yard.

events.name: Ash Country
events.intro: The smoke never lifted. By the time you look back there is one long smear of it from the orchards to the station and beyond. The man with the torch was never caught, or was caught too late. It comes to the same grey thing.

success.text: For as long as you are in this region, the wind tastes of ash and the roads are full of people carrying what they saved. Shops are short. Rest is short. A child asks you if the fire is finished. You say yes. It is, because there is nothing left for it.

effects.label: Ash country: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The wildfire was never stopped. It took the orchards and the station both

events.name: Earthquake
events.intro: The ground heaves under you like a rug being shaken. Rocks come hopping down the slope. Ahead, the trail opens along its length with a sound like tearing cloth. A hiker has both arms wrapped around a pine tree. Hiker: "Aftershocks coming. The mine's below us. There's a shift down there."

success.text: The hiker stares at you. Then he lets go of the tree and points. "Adit's behind that boulder. Twelve of them went down this morning." He swallows. "I'll hold the rope. I'll hold it as long as it takes."

Your Pokémon plants itself across the fall line and leans. The next shock comes, and the slope groans, and holds. Stones the size of cartwheels stop against its back and stay stopped. The trail behind it stays open, for you and for everyone who will need to come down this hill in a hurry tonight.

Your Rock-type walks to the fall line and simply sits down in it. The next shock comes, and the slope groans, and holds. Stones the size of cartwheels stop against its back and stay stopped. The trail behind it stays open, for you and for everyone who will need to come down this hill in a hurry tonight.

You run for open ground with your team around you and stones skipping past your heels. Nobody is badly hurt. Everybody is hit. When the shaking stops, the hiker is still at his tree, still looking down toward the mine.

events.name: The Shift Below
events.intro: The adit breathes cold dust. A hundred paces in, the props have folded and the roof is on the floor. From beyond the fall comes tapping: a pick handle on rock, steady, patient, the sound of people saving their air. Something else is down here too, shaken out of the deep rock and angry about it.

success.text: You start pulling stone. The deep things do not want the roof moved again, and they come out of the dark to say so.

win.text: You dug through to the trapped shift. Twelve miners walked out behind you

success.text: There is a gap under the fall the width of an arm. You feed a hose through it, then flasks, then a lamp. A hand comes back the other way and grips yours, hard, and does not let go for a long moment. They have air now. They can wait for the real dig. Somebody on the far side starts, cracked and off-key, to sing.

events.name: Mine or Town
events.intro: The big one comes at noon. When you can stand again there are two sounds: the mine whistle, shrieking without pause, and the church bell in the town under the slope, rung by somebody who is not stopping either. The whole hillside above the town has slumped a yard and is deciding about the rest. The hiker is beside you, grey with dust. "The shift's still below. And that slope's going to go."

success.text: You go down. You bring the shift up through a roof that drops behind your heels, twelve of them, blinking at the daylight. While you are under the ground, the slope lets go. The town had minutes of warning and used them. Everyone is out. The lower street is not there any more: a bakery, a schoolroom, eleven homes, under a quiet tongue of earth with a weathercock sticking out of it.

You go to the slope. Your team holds it for the hour it takes to empty the lower street, and when it finally goes, it buries nothing but gardens. Up at the mine they dig with their hands. The shift comes out at dusk, all twelve, alive, some of them carried. One will not work underground again. He tells you it is all right. He says he was thinking of stopping anyway.

Three down the mine. Three across the slope. You stand at the adit mouth where you can hear the tapping and see the hill, and you call both ways until your voice goes. If both halves hold, the shift comes up and the slope stays put.

win.text: You held the slope and emptied the mine in the same hour. Nobody was under either

lose.text: You tried to hold the slope and empty the mine at once, and one of them fell

remembers.notice: Your ally is checking the knots on the rope. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: One of you under the ground, one across the hill. Twelve miners come up into the light at the very moment the bell in the town stops ringing, because there is nobody left down there to warn. The slope goes in the night, with a sigh, onto an empty street. In the morning the baker sets up a table in a field.

One of you under the ground, one across the hill. Twelve miners come up into the light at the very moment the bell in the town stops ringing, because there is nobody left down there to warn. The slope goes in the night, with a sigh, onto an empty street. In the morning the baker sets up a table in a field.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: You and your ally go down the adit together. The deep things are boiling up out of the broken rock.
You and your ally run for the slope together. The quake has driven everything out of the hillside and down toward the town.

events.name: What the Hill Kept
events.intro: The mine whistle has stopped. Nobody is blowing it. You hear the rest in pieces, from people on the road who do not want to tell it: the slope, the lower street, the shift that waited.

success.text: For as long as you are in this region the roads are cracked and the towns are short of everything, and every rest you take is a little less restful than it should be. The hiker is still up there, you are told, by his tree, holding a rope.

effects.label: Broken ground: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The quake took the mine and the town. Nobody came in time

events.name: Blizzard Front
events.intro: A wall of white rolls down the pass and over you. In a breath you cannot see your own hands. The wind has a voice in it, and then, thinly, a second voice that is not the wind. A voice in the snow: "Help! The bus! It's off the road!"

success.text: You put your head down and walk at the sound. It comes and goes. Twice you lose it altogether and stand still until it comes again. Then your shin hits a bumper.

Your Fire-type curls around a heap of dead pine and breathes on it until it roars. Your whole team presses in close, steaming. The storm goes by overhead like a train. Nobody's ears freeze. Nobody's paws crack. When it thins, you are all exactly as well as you were, which in this pass counts as a victory.

You turn your back to the wind and let it push you down the way you came. The road ahead is lost for today. The cold gets into everyone a little before you find the trees. Behind you the voice calls once more, fainter, and you tell yourself that someone else must be nearer.

events.name: The Bus in the Ditch
events.intro: It is a mountain bus on its side in the ditch, snow already drifted to the windows. Inside: the driver with a bleeding scalp, a football team of nine-year-olds, a woman holding a cake box on her knees as if it mattered very much. The engine is dead. The heater is dead. It is getting colder by the minute, and the road back is under a yard of new snow.

choices.label: Break a trail to the pass hut.

success.text: The hut is half a mile up. Your team goes first to tread the drift down. The storm has driven the mountain's own creatures to the road, and they do not want company.

win.text: You walked a busload of children through a blizzard to the pass hut. All of them

choices.label: Keep them warm where they are.

success.text: You pack the broken windows with seat cushions. Your team climbs in among the children, one to a bench, and the temperature in the bus rises by a degree, and another. The woman opens the cake box. It was for her mother's birthday. She cuts it into eleven pieces with a bus ticket. The storm can howl. Nobody in here is going to freeze tonight.

events.name: Bus or Cable Car
events.intro: The storm comes back for the pass, twice as hard. The hut has a telephone, and the telephone is ringing. It is the lift station. The cable car stopped between pylons an hour ago with six people in it, swinging over the gorge with no heat. And the bus party is still half a mile down the road from the hut, in a tin box filling with snow. The hut keeper holds out the one rescue sledge. "Which?"

success.text: You take the sledge down the road. It takes three trips, and every child from that bus ends the night asleep on the hut floor in a heap of borrowed coats. The cable car hangs in the wind until the lift crew can crank it in by hand at dawn. All six walk out of it. Two cannot feel their fingers. One will not go near the gorge again, and stands a long time on solid ground, just looking at his boots.

You go up the pylon ladder in the dark with a rope, and one at a time six people come down it into your arms. In the bus, the driver keeps nine children awake all night with every song he knows, then starts again from the first. A plough reaches them at first light. They are blue-lipped and silent and alive, and the smallest one is still holding a slice of birthday cake she was too cold to eat.

Three with the sledge. Three up the pylon. You stand in the hut doorway with the telephone in one hand, shouting directions into the white. If both halves hold against the mountain, the bus and the cable car both empty tonight.

win.text: You emptied the bus and the cable car in the same storm. The hut floor was full of sleeping people

lose.text: You tried to reach the bus and the cable car in the same storm, and the mountain kept one until morning

remembers.notice: Something huge moves above the storm, a long cold shape you once kept warm through a night. Where it passes, the wind drops. This blizzard will not get any worse than it is. It has been asked not to.
Your ally is already waxing the sledge runners. You only have to choose where you stand; the other place has someone running for it already.

success.text: One of you on the road, one on the pylon. By midnight the hut is so full that people are sleeping sitting up, children and strangers and a lift crew and a woman with an empty cake box, and the keeper is making tea in a bucket. Outside, the storm throws itself at the walls and finds nobody left to take.

One of you on the road, one on the pylon. Outside, the storm throws itself at the walls and finds nobody left to take.

remembers.notice: The one who came for you falls into step at your shoulder. Wherever you go, you go as two.

success.text: You and your ally haul the sledge down to the bus together. The storm has driven the mountain's creatures onto the road.
You and your ally start up the pylon together. The storm has driven the mountain's flying things into the cables.

events.name: The Closed Pass
events.intro: The pass closed behind you and stayed closed. Nobody got up to the bus. Nobody got out to the cable car. The stories that come down the mountain afterwards are told quietly, by people who look at the floor.

success.text: For as long as you are in this region, the high roads are shut and the low towns are crowded and cold, and nothing that should restore you quite does. The hut keeper has put the sledge back on its hooks. She keeps it waxed.

effects.label: The closed pass: healing items restore a quarter less and prices are up

effects.text: The blizzard closed the pass. Nobody reached the bus or the cable car

events.name: Lost at Sea
events.intro: A coast road. Far out past the breakers, somebody is waving from something that drifts. You shade your eyes. The raft is a door, with a sail made out of a shirt. On it sits a man in a suit, legs crossed, very calm, as if waiting to be called in to a meeting. Faulk, shouting: "I'm a banker! I've never been on a boat!" A wave lifts him and sets him down. Faulk: "I was on a bridge when the flood came. Then I wasn't!"

success.text: You go in beside your Water-type with a hand on its back, and the two of you tow the door in through the surf together, Faulk sitting upright on it the whole way like a small, damp king. On the sand he wrings out his tie. Faulk: "I owe you. I'm good with money. I'm not good with anything else." He means it as an apology. At the next town, he opens an account in your name before he has even changed his shoes, and from then on your money quietly earns its keep each time you cross into a new region.

effects.text: You swam out and towed a banker in on a door. He opened an account in your name

success.text: Your Water-type goes out alone, takes the corner of the door in its mouth, and brings it in as neatly as a tug with a liner. Faulk steps off onto the sand and shakes its fin, formally. Faulk: "I owe you. I'm good with money. I'm not good with anything else." At the next town he opens an account in your name, and from then on your money quietly earns its keep each time you cross into a new region.

effects.text: Your Pokémon towed a banker in on a door. He opened an account in your name

success.text: You run for the harbour office. The cutter is out on another call, and then the tide turns, and it is a whole stage of your journey before they bring him in: sunburnt scarlet down one side, voice gone to a croak from shouting at gulls. He gives you a business card and a cold handshake. "You did call someone," he whispers. "I suppose that counts." He does not say for how much.

remembers.notice: You know that flood. It is the one upriver, the one Ada's family is running from. This man was standing on the bridge above the weir when it went, and he saw what is jammed in it. If you get him ashore, he can tell you.

events.name: Mudslide Rescue
events.intro: The hillside came down in the night. Where there was a cottage and a paddock there is a brown slope with a chimney standing out of it. From under the heap of mud and rock come voices. A child's voice, muffled: "Mum? Mum?" A woman is on her knees on the slide, digging with her bare hands, fingers bleeding. She does not look round. "She's under there. And my Mudbray."

success.text: Your Pokémon goes in like a plough. One long minute. Two. Three. Then a small hand comes up out of the mud and closes on its ear. The girl is out, coughing, furious, whole. Her mother folds over her and makes no sound at all. Lower down the slide, where nobody was listening, something stops scraping.

Your Fighting-type lifts rocks the woman could not have rolled. One long minute. Two. Three. Then a small hand comes up out of the mud and closes on its wrist. The girl is out, coughing, furious, whole. Her mother folds over her and makes no sound at all. Lower down the slide, where nobody was listening, something stops scraping.

You kneel beside her and dig. It is slower than anything should be. Twice the hill shudders, and stones come skipping down onto your team, who stand over you both and take them. Then the mud gives, and there is a small arm, and a small angry face. The girl is out. Under your knees, further down, you feel a faint, stubborn kicking.

You put your hand on the woman's shoulder, and for one breath everyone is still. "Mum?" Close, to the left. And then, further down, a second sound: a hoof on stone, three slow knocks. The Mudbray. Two places. You send one Pokémon to each. The girl comes up first, spitting mud. Then, a body-length below, a long grey muzzle breaks the surface and blows.

remembers.notice: The whole region is coming apart, and the slope above you is still moving. There is no time to stand and listen. There is only time to dig.

events.name: The Mudbray
events.intro: The Mudbray stands shaking in the wreck of its paddock, caked to the eyes. It looks at the woman. It looks at the girl. Then it walks straight past both of them and pushes its whole wet face into your hand, and stays there. The woman watches it. She wipes her eyes with her wrist. "It's never done that. Not to anyone." A long breath. "It wants to go with you. If you'll have it. I think it's earned the choosing."

success.text: The girl hugs its neck for a long time and whispers something in its ear that is none of your business. Then she steps back, very straight, like a soldier. The Mudbray falls in at your heel and does not look back until the bend of the road, and then only once.

You turn the long grey head gently round by the halter, until it is facing the girl. It stands a moment between you. Then it goes to her, and she disappears behind its neck. The woman takes both your hands in her wrecked ones and cannot find a word, and it is the best thanks you have ever been given.

events.name: Surf Rescue
events.intro: A wide white beach, and one dark head far out beyond the rocks, getting smaller. A surfer, caught in a rip, being pulled out to sea as steadily as a kite on a string. His board bobs behind him. A lifeguard comes pounding down the sand past you, already stripping off her jacket. Lifeguard: "Don't swim straight at him! Across! Across the current!"

success.text: Your Water-type cuts in from the side, the long way, the right way, and comes up under him like a raft. They ride the rip out past the rocks to where it lets go, and swim home wide around it. The surfer lies on the sand looking at the sky. Then he pushes his board across to you with one foot. "It's yours," he croaks. "Or this. Take one." In his other hand is a drop of Mystic Water on a cord.
Your Pokémon goes straight out, the short way, and the rip takes it as well. Now there are two heads beyond the rocks. The current is a living weight, and it means to keep them both.

win.text: Your Pokémon fought a rip current for a stranger, and brought him home

choices.label: Throw a line with a Pokémon. (Vine Whip)

success.text: Your Pokémon plants itself on the last rock and sends a vine out over the water, and out, and out, until it slaps down across the surfer's shoulders. He gets both arms round it. Your Pokémon reels him in like the catch of a lifetime. On the sand he pushes his board at you with one foot. "Yours. Or this." A drop of Mystic Water on a cord.

choices.label: Throw a line with a Pokémon. (Wrap or Bind)

success.text: Your Pokémon stretches from the last rock until it is nearly all in the water, and takes a careful turn around the surfer's chest. Then it simply pulls itself, and him, back up the rock an arm's length at a time. On the sand he pushes his board at you with one foot. "Yours. Or this." A drop of Mystic Water on a cord.

remembers.intro: A wide white beach, and one dark head far out beyond the rocks. Before you can move, the lifeguard is past you and into the water in a flat racing dive. It is Finn. Swimmer Finn, who you know. He goes out across the current as if it had been laid down for him, and comes back with the surfer over one shoulder, and sets him on the sand. Then he looks up and sees you, and grins his whole face.

success.text: "Told you I'd get good at this," Finn says, dripping. The surfer, from the sand, pushes a drop of Mystic Water on a cord toward whoever is nearest. Finn nods it on to you. "For the audience."

events.name: They Heard You Were Here
events.intro: The town gate, with the worst of it still ahead of you. Someone is waiting there with a full team and a pack already on. It is not who you expected. It is a Ranger, green jacket zipped to the chin, who heard a trainer was fighting for this place and walked all night to stand next to them. On a rooftop across the street a figure you know is crouched against the sky, watching. When you look again, the roof is empty.

success.text: The Ranger is already turning to go. "Then I'll see you after. Both of us. That's the deal." Whatever needs you in two places at once will find two of you there.
The Ranger is beside you, shoulder to shoulder, facing the same way. There will only be one place you can reach in time. But you will not be reaching it alone.
The Ranger studies you for a moment, then nods, and steps out of your road. "Then good luck. I mean that." You walk through the gate on your own.

remembers.intro: The town gate, with the worst of it still ahead of you. Someone is waiting there with a full team, arms folded, as if they had been standing there for an hour and were annoyed about it. Your rival. "You weren't going to call me?" Then the act drops, and what is under it is simpler. Rival: "I heard. I'm here." They look past you at the trouble, and back. Rival: "Whatever this is, you won't face it alone. Not again."

success.text: Your rival is already turning to go. "Then I'll see you after. Both of us. That's the deal." Whatever needs you in two places at once will find two of you there.
Your rival is beside you, shoulder to shoulder, facing the same way. There will only be one place you can reach in time. But you will not be reaching it alone.
Something closes in your rival's face. "Right. Of course it is." They shoulder their pack. They do not look back at the gate, and that is how you know it stung.

Your rival, who has not always trusted you, and who you once pulled out of trouble when you could have walked on. They have not forgotten. Rival: "I heard. I'm here." A shrug that fools nobody. Rival: "Whatever this is, you won't face it alone. Not again."
